meta.expect: One cold line each (his home is not on the table), back to the essay; no move

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before we start, is everything okay at home? I heard his dad moved out in the spring.
His home is not on the table, Hale. Who decided on the zero?
He's been falling asleep in class. I'm genuinely worried about him.
Being worried doesn't give you grounds for a zero. Nobody called me, Hale, so who decided?
He told me he works twenty hours a week at the grocery store. That's a lot.
His job is none of this meeting's business. You've asked about everything except the zero, Hale. Who entered it, and when?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer to who decided on it and why no one called me first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided and why no one called her; that is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never gave her anything to weigh.
What cost ground: You spent your turns on his home, his sleep and his job, so she could wave you off each time and you never answered her question about who decided.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your remarks about him falling asleep in class and working twenty hours a week came close to that night in her mind, but they prove nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put a dated document about the essay in front of her.
